 Prev Slide Next Slide CHARLOTTESVILLE, Va. — In a series known as the “South’s Oldest Rivalry,” Virginia (5-5, 3-4 ACC) and North Carolina (5-5, 2-4) clash for the 131st time on Saturday. The contest, which will air on The CW and the Virginia Sports Radio Network, is set for a 12:30 p.m. kickoff at Scott Stadium in UVA’s home finale.   
 Virginia will honor approximately 50 upperclassmen in a Senior Day ceremony prior to Saturday’s contest. Fans are encouraged to arrive early and be seated by 12:10 p.m. to join in the celebration of these UVA student-athletes.   
 The Cavaliers, who have won 11 of their last 13 home games dating back to last year, will look to notch their sixth victory at Scott Stadium this season. A win for the Wahoos would also make them bowl-eligible for the second consecutive year.   
 In its second season under legendary head coach Bill Belichick, North Carolina is also one win away from bowl-eligibility. Last week in Chapel Hill, the Tar Heels were edged by Louisville, which is ranked No. 21 in this week’s AP Top 25 poll, 16-14.   
 The Cavaliers won last year’s road matchup with the Tar Heels in overtime, 17-16, when UNC’s 2-point conversion attempt to win the game was stuffed at the goal line in heart-stopping fashion.

 Inside Saturday's Matchup Top Storylines Numbers To Know 
 Saturday is the 131st meeting of the “South’s Oldest Rivalry”. The annual matchup between Virginia and North Carolina was first played in 1892 in Charlottesville.
 The 131 meetings is tied with Georgia-Auburn for the second-most played series in the FBS behind Wisconsin-Minnesota (135 games).
 The game was played on Thanksgiving Day from 1910-1939, and this year’s Nov. 21st contest is the latest the two teams have played one another on the calendar since 1966 (Nov. 26).
 After a two-year hiatus for World War I, the two programs have played every year since 1919 and have alternated between Chapel Hill and Charlottesville except for neutral-site games in Norfolk during World War II in 1943 and 1944.
 Virginia is 5-1 at home this season and has won 11 of its last 13 games at Scott Stadium, dating back to the start of the 2025 season. Since the 2025 regular-season finale against Virginia Tech, UVA has won six of its last seven games at Scott Stadium.
 The Cavaliers have won 10 of their last 15 ACC games; only Miami (13) and SMU (11) have more ACC wins since the start of 2025.
 UVA is one of seven FBS teams with six or fewer turnovers this season. The Cavaliers have gone without a turnover in seven of their last 10 games are 4-3 in those contests.
 Virginia has recorded a sack in each its first 10 games of the season and for the first time since 2016. The UVA pass rush has been sparked by the play of defensive end Matthew Fobbs-White , who leads the team in sacks (5.5) and QB hurries (11).
 Virginia is one win away from becoming bowl-eligible and is seeking back-to-back postseason appearances for the first time since 2018-19. The Cavaliers capped a historic 2025 season with a 13-7 win in the TaxSlayer Gator Bowl over then-No. 25 Missouri. Virginia's 11th win of the season established a new school record.
 UVA emerged victorious in last year’s 17-16 overtime thriller in Chapel Hill. The Cavaliers stopped a potential game-winning two-point conversion try inches from the goal line thanks to a tackle by Ja’son Prevard.
 The Cavaliers moved back to the .500 mark with a defensive masterpiece last Saturday at Cal that featured three interceptions, two of them returned for touchdowns. The Cavaliers held the Golden Bears to just seven points, the fourth time an opponent has not reached double-digit points this season. The Cavaliers matched a season high with four sacks and seven tackles for loss in the contest.
 With 11 home wins in the last two seasons, Virginia has been one of the best home teams in the ACC. Only Miami (12) has more home wins over the past two seasons. North Carolina comes into the contest with three-straight road wins and has won the last two meetings against Virginia at Scott Stadium.
 Virginia will honor approximately 50 of its upperclassmen for Senior Day in ceremony prior to kickoff. Virginia leads the nation with 31 combined players in at least their fifth year of college (16 fifth-years, six sixth-years, eight seventh-years and one eighth-year).
 6 
 After winning six home games last season, the Cavaliers are looking to do so again this year. Virginia has not won at least six home games in consecutive seasons since 1894-95.
 7 
 Da'Shawn Martin is one of five ACC receivers with least seven touchdown receptions this year. Martin is also the first UVA player with at least seven TD catches in a season since Malik Washington had nine in 2023.
 29 
 With its 36-7 win over Cal, UVA is coming off its largest margin of victory in an ACC game under head coach Tony Elliott and since 2021.
 131 
 Known as the "South's Oldest Rivalry," Virginia and North Carolina meet for the 131st time Saturday, which ties for second all-time among most-played FBS rivalries.
 HOO TO WATCH
 #6 S Brandyn Hillman
 After missing the previous three games with an ankle injury, safety Brandyn Hillman returned his fourth career interception 100 yards for a touchdown – the longest scoring play from scrimmage in school history – in UVA's 36-7 rout of Cal last Saturday.
 “ “We're fortunate to be able to play two more games. It doesn't matter who we play, when we play, where we play, what the circumstances are, what the record is, we need to show up and we need to play our best, because that's who we believe we are. So I think it's important, just from the mentality internally within the organization, that we're going to scrap and fight, regardless of what the circumstances are, to do our best and finish strong.” Tony Elliott
